name: Counting Sort
description: Non-comparison sort that counts occurrences of each value, uses running sum to determine positions, then builds the output array. Extremely fast for integers in a small range.
aim: Sort by counting how many times each value appears, converting counts to cumulative positions, then placing each element at its determined position in the output.
howItWorks: Create count array of size k+1, initialize to 0
Accumulate: count[i] += count[i-1] to get positions
Place each element in output: output[count[arr[i]]-1] = arr[i]
Copy output back to original array

time.averageCase: k = range of input values, n = number of elements

complexity.spaceDescription: Count array of size k = max value

realWorld: Radix sort uses counting sort as a subroutine
whenToUse: Input integers in a small known range [0..k]
k = O(n) — range comparable to array size
alternatives: Radix Sort — extends counting sort to multi-digit numbers
Bucket Sort — works on floating-point numbers
Comparison sorts — when range is too large relative to n
